scenes.text: Ask ChatGPT about your company's leave policy, and it has no idea. [1] It was never trained on your documents. [2] The fix is called RAG.
Think of an exam. [1] A normal L L M is a closed book exam. It answers from memory, and might guess. [2] RAG is an open book exam. It looks up the right pages first, then answers.

RAG stands for retrieval augmented generation. [1] It means, find the right information first, then answer. [2] Retrieve. Search your documents. [3] Augment. Add what you found to the prompt. [4] Generate. The L L M writes the answer, using it.

data.definition: Find the right information first, then let the AI answer using it.

scenes.text: Here's the flow, with an H R policy bot. [1] An employee asks, how many leave days do I get? [2] The question is turned into an embedding. [3] The vector database finds the matching paragraph in the H R policy. [4] That paragraph is added to the prompt, along with the question. [5] And the L L M answers. Twenty four days a year, and it cites the policy.

data.heading: RAG, step by step
nodes: “How many leave days do I get?”

scenes.text: Where is RAG used? [1] Company chatbots that answer from internal documents. [2] Bank and telecom support bots that follow the latest rules. [3] And chat with your P D F tools, for notes, contracts and research papers.

Why is RAG so popular? [1] Fresh. Update the documents, and answers update instantly, with no retraining. [2] Private. Your data stays in your own database. [3] Trustworthy. It can show the source for every answer. [4] And cheap, compared to training a model.
Myth! [1] With RAG, the AI never makes mistakes. [2] Not quite. If the search finds the wrong paragraph, the answer will be wrong. Good RAG needs good search, and clean documents.

data.myth: With RAG, the AI never makes mistakes.
data.fact: If retrieval finds the wrong text, the answer is wrong. Good RAG needs good search and clean docs.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! In RAG, what does the R stand for? [1] Pause and think. <pause 3.2> [2] Retrieval! Find the right information first. Comment R if you got it!

Recap. [1] RAG is an open book exam for AI. [2] Retrieve the right information. [3] Augment the prompt with it. [4] Generate an answer, with sources. [5] Next episode. Prompting, RAG, or fine tuning. Which one should you use, and when? Follow AI Maastaaru!
